6	    "finding": "👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: A name made only of replaced or trailing characters gives a folder name ending in a space**\n\n`validateWorkspaceName` accepts a name like `?`, `...` or `-`. In `newWorkspaceFolderName`, `?` turns into `-`, and the trailing-strip regex then removes it, so `safe` ends up as `\"\"`. The function then returns `\"Kaipu Record — \"`, which ends in a space: the same trailing space the doc comment says Windows refuses. On macOS a second name like that (for example `*`) collides with the first folder, and `create` refuses it as `exists`. A possible fix: when `safe` is empty, fall back to a placeholder, or strip the trailing space from the whole result. Another option is to reject such names in validation.\n\n<!-- wachi:finding -->",

9	        "author": "csdev19",
10	        "body": "Fixed in 886d67f0. Runs of unsafe characters now become one dash and only dots and spaces are stripped from the end, so `?` gives `Kaipu Record — -`. A name that leaves nothing (`...`) falls back to `workspace`. Tests in `workspace-name.test.ts` check the folder name never ends in a space. `?` and `*` still map to the same folder; `create` then refuses the second as \"exists\" and the dialog says so, which I think is the right outcome."

Take a pending entry whose folder is reachable but has no `identity.json` (`previous` is missing). `edit` writes a fresh identity at line 581 with the entry's id and the new name. If `update` then throws, that file stays on disk. The next probe finds an identity with the matching id and adopts it, so the change that was refused shows up again. Calling `removeIdentity(entry.path)` in the non-ok case would undo it the way `create`'s `undo` does.\n\n<!-- wachi:finding -->",

findings.title: An unrelated offline edit turns the deferred color upgrade into a write of the folder's color
findings.body: `edit` deletes `pendingColorUpgrade` and sets `pendingIdentity` (lines 629-631) even when the user changed only the name. On reconnect, the `pendingIdentity` branch (lines 663-672) writes name, color and initials from the cache over the folder's file. The cached color is the app-supplied brand color, not one the user chose. So if another Mac recolored the folder while this one was away and the user then renames it here, that recolor is overwritten without a choice from anyone. The new test at `registry-create-edit.test.ts:206` pins the rename-wins case but not the color. Consider clearing `pendingColorUpgrade` only when the patch includes a color. When the patch has only a name, keep it, and have the pending-identity write skip the color unless `isOldDefault`.

contracts.action: Deferred brand-color upgrade is written to identity.json only if the folder still holds the old Default and rose
contracts.equivalent_path: The pendingIdentity path in availability (registry.ts:663-680), which writes the cached identity over the folder's file unconditionally.
contracts.before_after: Before: the upgrade set pendingIdentity, so a reconnected folder that another Mac had renamed or recolored was overwritten by the cached color. After: pendingColorUpgrade writes only when isOldDefault(file) is true. Otherwise the stale branch (lines 691-708) adopts the folder's file and clears the marker. The write uses {...file, color: entry.color}, so it touches only the color. edit() clears the marker and takes ownership. Both probe branches clear it after a successful write.
contracts.visible_effect: The Default workspace keeps whatever name and color the folder holds. The brand color appears only when nobody changed the folder.
contracts.failure_mode: If writeIdentity throws, the marker stays and the next probe retries. Probes are not serialized, so a probe that read the file before an edit's write can write the old name back. This is the same window the existing pendingIdentity branch has, and it is narrow.

contracts.action: Change folder… on the folder the workspace already points at returns early, with no transaction
contracts.equivalent_path: relocateActive in switch-transaction.ts, which the active-workspace path used before. It asks windows to prepare, bumps the generation and drops captures.
contracts.before_after: Before: picking the current folder ran the full transaction for a no-op. After: checkRelocate runs first, then a same-path early return gives {ok:true, entry} with no window prepare, no generation bump and no capture drop. relocateFolder in index.ts then still calls reg.availability, so a hand-deleted identity.json is rewritten, then refreshTitles and broadcastState.
contracts.visible_effect: The user sees the 'folder changed' toast with nothing remounting and no unsaved-changes prompt.
contracts.failure_mode: If checkRelocate or availability throws, the IPC call rejects. The renderer now catches this and shows relocateUncertain, in the dialog or as a toast.

contracts.action: checkRelocate accepts a Kaipu-items folder with no identity.json for a pendingInit workspace
contracts.equivalent_path: add() at registry.ts:756-817, which mints an identity for a folder without one. relocate must keep the registered id.
contracts.before_after: Before: such a folder was refused as has-items-no-identity, which stranded a pendingInit Default whose drive came back at a new mount path. After: for a pendingInit entry only, the folder is accepted. relocate() then repoints the path, and the probe in relocateFolder writes identity.json under the registered id (the no-identity branch at lines 726-746) and clears pendingInit.
contracts.visible_effect: The user can recover a Default workspace that was registered while its drive was unplugged.
contracts.failure_mode: Any folder with a .kaipu directory and no identity is accepted for a pendingInit entry. The user's pick is the only evidence it is the right folder. Other workspaces keep the stricter rule. A folder holding a different workspace's identity is still refused as 'different'.

contracts.action: Rejected create, edit and relocate IPC calls now show an 'uncertain' message
contracts.equivalent_path: The refusal path, where a returned {ok:false, reason} sets refusal or folderError. The new catch uses distinct `*-uncertain` reasons and the relocateUncertain key.
contracts.before_after: Before: a rejection left the dialog silent, or in the context's changeFolder an unhandled rejection from `void changeFolder(...)`. After: the dialog's submit and changeFolder catch it and show an alert. The context's changeFolder shows a toast. busy and relocating are reset in `finally`.
contracts.visible_effect: The user is told to check the Workspaces list or the folder before retrying, instead of seeing 'failed'. The Save and Create buttons come back enabled.
contracts.failure_mode: checkLocation's `.then` at line 95 still has no catch. That is existing code and out of scope. Because the dialog stays open after an uncertain create, a retry can hit name-taken if the first call did register the workspace. The message tells the user to check first.

thread_replies.reply: The main case is fixed. `checkRelocate` now accepts a folder with `.kaipu/` items and no identity for a `pendingInit` entry (registry.ts:843-850), and the probe after the move writes the identity under the registered id. A test covers it. The second half of the comment is not done: a moved folder that holds another, unregistered id is still refused as `different` for a `pendingInit` entry, while `availability` would adopt that id. That was only a suggested extension, so I'm not holding this open on it.
Not changed in this part. `relocateActive` still drops pending captures on a real relocation. Only the same-folder case now skips the transaction. Reply if you want to keep dropping the capture.

Fixed. `relocateWorkspace` returns early when the picked folder is the current one (relocate.ts:42-43). No window is asked to prepare, the generation is not bumped and captures are kept. The caller's probe still runs. `relocate.test.ts` covers it.
Fixed. The 'Move to' sentence is gone from `relocateNotWorkspace` in en.json and es.json, and the dialog test now asserts the text does not mention it.

Fixed. The dialog's `changeFolder` and the context's `changeFolder` both catch a rejection. The dialog shows `relocateUncertain` in the folder-error alert and the context shows a toast. The message says the result is unknown rather than 'failed', which fits a rejection after main may have applied the change.
Fixed. The test now resolves a relocate, checks that Save stays disabled, then changes the color and checks that Save becomes enabled.

input.summary: The change holds up. The deferred color upgrade now has its own `pendingColorUpgrade` marker, so it yields to a folder that changed while it was away. Same-folder relocation returns early. A `pendingInit` workspace can be repointed at a folder with Kaipu items and no identity. Rejected create, edit and relocate calls now show an 'uncertain' message in en and es. The tests assert what their names say. I found one consider-level issue: an offline rename clears the deferred upgrade and later writes the cached brand color over the folder's file, which could overwrite another Mac's recolor. Four threads are addressed: the `pendingInit` relocate, the same-folder relocate, the 'Move to' text, and the rejected relocate. The test-name thread is addressed too. One thread, on relocating the active workspace dropping the pending capture, is still open and lives outside this part's files.

findings.title: An unrelated offline edit turns the deferred color upgrade into a write of the folder's color
findings.body: `edit` deletes `pendingColorUpgrade` and sets `pendingIdentity` (lines 629-631) even when the user changed only the name. On reconnect, the `pendingIdentity` branch (lines 663-672) writes name, color and initials from the cache over the folder's file. The cached color is the app-supplied brand color, not one the user chose. So if another Mac recolored the folder while this one was away and the user then renames it here, that recolor is overwritten without a choice from anyone. The new test at `registry-create-edit.test.ts:206` pins the rename-wins case but not the color. Consider clearing `pendingColorUpgrade` only when the patch includes a color. When the patch has only a name, keep it, and have the pending-identity write skip the color unless `isOldDefault`.

contracts.action: Deferred brand-color upgrade is written to identity.json only if the folder still holds the old Default and rose
contracts.equivalent_path: The pendingIdentity path in availability (registry.ts:663-680), which writes the cached identity over the folder's file unconditionally.
contracts.before_after: Before: the upgrade set pendingIdentity, so a reconnected folder that another Mac had renamed or recolored was overwritten by the cached color. After: pendingColorUpgrade writes only when isOldDefault(file) is true. Otherwise the stale branch (lines 691-708) adopts the folder's file and clears the marker. The write uses {...file, color: entry.color}, so it touches only the color. edit() clears the marker and takes ownership. Both probe branches clear it after a successful write.
contracts.visible_effect: The Default workspace keeps whatever name and color the folder holds. The brand color appears only when nobody changed the folder.
contracts.failure_mode: If writeIdentity throws, the marker stays and the next probe retries. Probes are not serialized, so a probe that read the file before an edit's write can write the old name back. This is the same window the existing pendingIdentity branch has, and it is narrow.

contracts.action: Change folder… on the folder the workspace already points at returns early, with no transaction
contracts.equivalent_path: relocateActive in switch-transaction.ts, which the active-workspace path used before. It asks windows to prepare, bumps the generation and drops captures.
contracts.before_after: Before: picking the current folder ran the full transaction for a no-op. After: checkRelocate runs first, then a same-path early return gives {ok:true, entry} with no window prepare, no generation bump and no capture drop. relocateFolder in index.ts then still calls reg.availability, so a hand-deleted identity.json is rewritten, then refreshTitles and broadcastState.
contracts.visible_effect: The user sees the 'folder changed' toast with nothing remounting and no unsaved-changes prompt.
contracts.failure_mode: If checkRelocate or availability throws, the IPC call rejects. The renderer now catches this and shows relocateUncertain, in the dialog or as a toast.

contracts.action: checkRelocate accepts a Kaipu-items folder with no identity.json for a pendingInit workspace
contracts.equivalent_path: add() at registry.ts:756-817, which mints an identity for a folder without one. relocate must keep the registered id.
contracts.before_after: Before: such a folder was refused as has-items-no-identity, which stranded a pendingInit Default whose drive came back at a new mount path. After: for a pendingInit entry only, the folder is accepted. relocate() then repoints the path, and the probe in relocateFolder writes identity.json under the registered id (the no-identity branch at lines 726-746) and clears pendingInit.
contracts.visible_effect: The user can recover a Default workspace that was registered while its drive was unplugged.
contracts.failure_mode: Any folder with a .kaipu directory and no identity is accepted for a pendingInit entry. The user's pick is the only evidence it is the right folder. Other workspaces keep the stricter rule. A folder holding a different workspace's identity is still refused as 'different'.

contracts.action: Rejected create, edit and relocate IPC calls now show an 'uncertain' message
contracts.equivalent_path: The refusal path, where a returned {ok:false, reason} sets refusal or folderError. The new catch uses distinct `*-uncertain` reasons and the relocateUncertain key.
contracts.before_after: Before: a rejection left the dialog silent, or in the context's changeFolder an unhandled rejection from `void changeFolder(...)`. After: the dialog's submit and changeFolder catch it and show an alert. The context's changeFolder shows a toast. busy and relocating are reset in `finally`.
contracts.visible_effect: The user is told to check the Workspaces list or the folder before retrying, instead of seeing 'failed'. The Save and Create buttons come back enabled.
contracts.failure_mode: checkLocation's `.then` at line 95 still has no catch. That is existing code and out of scope. Because the dialog stays open after an uncertain create, a retry can hit name-taken if the first call did register the workspace. The message tells the user to check first.
